# Spec: Project Memory System

**ID:** memory-system
**Priority:** Must
**Traces to problem in brief:** *Currently each `cycle` arrives blind — no memory of how the project evolved, what was rejected, what preferences the human stated. After a long pause the user must reconstruct context manually from `state.json`, `.transcripts/`, and the artifact directory. This violates the framework's autonomy promise.*

**Type:** Multi-release feature (v0.4.5 → v0.4.6 → v0.5.0)
**Generated by:** ultrareview of 4 parallel design agents (2026-05-29)

---

## User Story (top-level)

As **the human collaborator running IAgentek on a real project**, I want **the framework to remember what the project is, what was decided, what I told it I prefer, and where it stands at any moment — automatically, with zero manual commands**, so that **I can pause for three weeks, come back, and feel that the system never lost the thread**.

---

## Release plan

The feature splits into three releases. Each is independently shippable and additive.

| Release | Date target | Scope | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| **v0.4.5** | T+3 days | Two preexisting bug fixes that any memory system requires as foundation | Low |
| **v0.4.6** | T+10 days | `CONTEXT.md` + `HISTORY.md` + enriched `status`/`resume` (no LLM secondary, no PREFERENCES, no scribe) | Low |
| **v0.5.0** | T+25 days | `scribe` agent + `PREFERENCES.md` + breaking `CheckpointManager` signature + plugin slash commands | Medium (requires all 8 blocking security mitigations) |

The split is deliberate — v0.4.6 alone delivers ~80% of the emotional requirement ("everything is being saved") without opening the prompt-injection surface of an LLM-driven curator. v0.5.0 is gated on the 8 blocking mitigations from the red-team review.

# Release 1 — v0.4.5: Preexisting bug fixes

## User Story
As **any user of IAgentek**, I want **`state.json` to never get corrupted by a crash mid-write and approved checkpoints to never be lost in a crash before phase completion**, so that **I can trust `resume` after any kind of interruption**.

## AC

- [ ] **AC-1.1:** Given a `cycle` running, When the process is killed mid-`StateManager.save()`, Then `state.json` is left at its previous valid value AND no `.tmp` files leak past the next `load()`.
- [ ] **AC-1.2:** Given an antivirus / OneDrive briefly locks `state.json` during rename, When `save()` is called, Then the rename retries with backoff up to ~820ms before failing with a clear error message.
- [ ] **AC-1.3:** Given a checkpoint is approved but the process crashes before `markPhaseCompleted`, When the user runs `iagentek resume`, Then the orchestrator reconciles state automatically (no manual command, no token re-spend) and proceeds to the next phase.
- [ ] **AC-1.4:** Given a transcript exists on disk for a phase from <24h ago, When `runPhase` is invoked for that phase, Then the existing transcript is reused (logged as `♻ Reusing transcript from Xh ago`) instead of re-calling the LLM.
- [ ] **AC-1.5:** Given a project directory contains `state.json.<pid>.<hex>.tmp` files older than 60 seconds, When `StateManager.load()` is called, Then they are cleaned up automatically.

## Edge cases
- **Edge-1:** Disk full (ENOSPC) during save → `state.json` preserved at previous value, `.tmp` cleaned, clear error pointing user to free space.
- **Edge-2:** Readonly bit set on `state.json` → save fails with explicit message, existing state intact.
- **Edge-3:** OneDrive on-demand path with `.iagentek/` marked online-only → first save may be slow; warning suggested at `init` if path contains "OneDrive".
- **Edge-4:** Symlink at `state.json` → rename replaces the symlink itself (acceptable, documented).
- **Edge-5:** Two concurrent `cycle` processes for the same project → tmp filenames carry PID+random so no collision; last-writer-wins on rename (acceptable for v0.4.5; lockfile is v2 concern).
- **Edge-6:** Approve-then-crash-then-disk-full reconcile → state preserved, user can `resume` after freeing space, no silent data loss.

## NOT in scope of this release
- Any memory-system features (CONTEXT.md, HISTORY.md, PREFERENCES.md, scribe agent).
- Lockfile for concurrent execution prevention.
- Detection of duplicate `init` over an existing project.
- Any CLI message changes other than the new `♻ Reusing transcript...` line.

## Dependencies
- Specs that must exist first: none.
- External data/systems: none.

## Technical plan
See `plans/memory-bugfixes.md`.

## Files touched
- `packages/core/src/state/manager.ts` — atomic `save()` (tmp+fsync+rename+retry+cleanup).
- `packages/core/src/orchestrator/index.ts` — reconcile at start of `run()`, transcript reuse inside `runPhase`.
- `packages/core/src/checkpoints/manager.ts` — return `{ decision, notes }` (signature ready for v0.5.0; v0.4.5 only adds the field, callers still ignore it).
- `packages/core/src/flow/loader.ts` — validate `checkpoint.id` uniqueness across phases.
- `packages/core/test/state.atomic.test.ts` (new) — 10 test cases.
- `packages/core/test/orchestrator.reconcile.test.ts` (new) — 5 test cases.
- `packages/core/test/transcripts.reuse.test.ts` (new) — 4 test cases.

# Release 2 — v0.4.6: CONTEXT.md + HISTORY.md + enriched status/resume

## User Story
As **the human collaborator**, I want **a regenerable snapshot of the project state (`CONTEXT.md`) and an append-only log of every cycle event (`HISTORY.md`), written automatically with no commands**, so that **when I come back days later the system shows me exactly where I left off and what I told it**.

## AC

- [ ] **AC-2.1:** Given a `cycle` runs and a phase is approved, When `markPhaseCompleted` returns, Then `.iagentek/CONTEXT.md` is regenerated atomically (tmp+rename) AND `.iagentek/HISTORY.md` has a new append entry with timestamp, phase, agent, decision, and human notes.
- [ ] **AC-2.2:** Given any of the six write-through events fires (cycle_started, phase_started, phase_output_received, checkpoint_prompted, checkpoint_approved|rejected, phase_completed, cycle_completed), When the event occurs, Then `HISTORY.md` gets exactly one new entry, atomic on POSIX (single appendFileSync <4KB).
- [ ] **AC-2.3:** Given the user presses Ctrl-C mid-cycle, When the process exits via SIGINT handler, Then `HISTORY.md` gets a `cycle_interrupted` entry before the process dies (best-effort, sync).
- [ ] **AC-2.4:** Given `state.json` exists from v0.4.4 or earlier but `CONTEXT.md` does not, When the orchestrator starts, Then `CONTEXT.md` is bootstrapped silently from existing artifacts (brief, PRD, state) with header noting `<!-- bootstrapped from v0.4.4 state -->`.
- [ ] **AC-2.5:** Given `now() - state.updatedAt > 7 days`, When the user runs `cycle` or `resume`, Then the CLI prints the "Welcome back" block with: project summary from CONTEXT, last 5 events from HISTORY, human notes from last checkpoint, exact next-step command.
- [ ] **AC-2.6:** Given a phase completes, When the orchestrator finishes writing CONTEXT+HISTORY, Then the CLI prints `  ↳ Memory updated: HISTORY +1 entry, CONTEXT +N chars` before showing the next phase header.
- [ ] **AC-2.7:** Given the user runs `iagentek status`, When `CONTEXT.md` and `HISTORY.md` exist, Then `status` includes a "Memory" block showing last-updated times, history entry count, and (if applicable) "0 learned preferences" placeholder.
- [ ] **AC-2.8:** Given the user runs `iagentek context` (new command), When called, Then it prints `CONTEXT.md` to stdout with kleur color highlights, pipe-friendly.
- [ ] **AC-2.9:** Given `HISTORY.md` exceeds 500 entries OR 200 KB, When the next append would land, Then the orchestrator rotates: moves older entries to `.iagentek/.archive/history-YYYY-MM.md` and keeps the most recent 50 + an `## Archive` index in the main file.
- [ ] **AC-2.10:** Given `CONTEXT.md` candidate write is shorter than 200 bytes AND existing file is larger than 200 bytes, When the writer runs, Then the write is aborted with warning and `CONTEXT.md.prev` is preserved. (Anti-clobber, same heuristic family as `looksLikePlaceholder`.)

## Edge cases
- **Edge-1:** `HISTORY.md` corrupted by manual user edit → orchestrator never reads it for control flow (only `state.json` does); HISTORY is human-display only in v0.4.6. Tolerance to garbage lines.
- **Edge-2:** Disk full while writing CONTEXT → captured as ENOSPC, logged, cycle continues. CONTEXT is best-effort. HISTORY is still attempted because append is cheaper.
- **Edge-3:** User opens `PREFERENCES.md` (which doesn't exist yet in this release) → 404 expected; v0.4.6 does not create or reference this file.
- **Edge-4:** Project with `.iagentek/.history-archive/` already present from a future version downgrade → orchestrator ignores unknown dirs.
- **Edge-5:** Concurrent reads of `CONTEXT.md` during regeneration → tmp+rename guarantees readers see either the old or the new complete file, never partial.
- **Edge-6:** Timezone changes between sessions → all timestamps written as ISO-8601 UTC; display uses local TZ.

## NOT in scope of this release
- Scribe agent / `PREFERENCES.md` (deferred to v0.5.0).
- Any LLM secondary calls.
- Per-agent context-injection differences (all agents get full CONTEXT today; tailoring is v2).
- Plugin slash commands (deferred to v0.5.0).
- Lockfile for concurrent execution.
- Telemetry / `iagentek stats`.

## Dependencies
- Specs that must exist first: `v0.4.5` (atomic state, reconcile, transcript reuse).
- External data/systems: none.

## Technical plan
See `plans/memory-context-history.md`.

## Files touched
- `packages/core/src/memory/manager.ts` (new) — `MemoryManager` class: `ensureInitialized`, `recordCycleStart`, `recordPhaseStart`, `recordPhaseOutput`, `recordCheckpointPrompted`, `recordCheckpointDecision`, `recordPhaseCompleted`, `recordCycleEnd`, `recordInterrupted`.
- `packages/core/src/memory/writer.ts` (new) — atomic CONTEXT write (tmp+rename+size-guard+`.prev` backup); append-only HISTORY with fsync.
- `packages/core/src/memory/templates.ts` (new) — frontmatter and section templates for CONTEXT.md.
- `packages/core/src/memory/bootstrap.ts` (new) — backfill CONTEXT from existing `state.json` + brief + PRD when migrating from v0.4.4.
- `packages/core/src/orchestrator/index.ts` — inject `memory?: MemoryManager` in `OrchestratorOptions`; call hooks at 6 trigger points (additive, ~6 lines).
- `packages/core/src/checkpoints/manager.ts` — already returns `{ decision, notes }` from v0.4.5; orchestrator now uses `notes` to feed HISTORY.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/cycle.ts` — construct `MemoryManager`, install SIGINT handler.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/status.ts` — add "Memory" block + ">7 days welcome back" branch.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/resume.ts` — surface human notes from last checkpoint at top.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/context.ts` (new) — print CONTEXT.md.
- `packages/cli/src/bin/iagentek.ts` — register `context` command.
- Tests: 12+ new test cases covering atomic CONTEXT writes, HISTORY append safety, bootstrap from v0.4.4, SIGINT handling, rotation at threshold.

# Release 3 — v0.5.0: Scribe agent + PREFERENCES.md

## User Story
As **the human collaborator**, I want **the framework to silently learn my preferences (which test runner, which package manager, which stack choices) as I approve checkpoints, and apply them to all future agents without me re-stating them every cycle**, so that **the system truly gets to know my project the way a long-term teammate would**.

## AC

- [ ] **AC-3.1:** Given a checkpoint is approved with notes, When the orchestrator finishes recording the approval, Then the `scribe` agent is invoked automatically with the phase transcript + notes + current `PREFERENCES.md` as input.
- [ ] **AC-3.2:** Given the scribe responds with valid `memory:add | memory:update | memory:deprecate | memory:none` blocks, When the orchestrator parses, Then up to 3 valid mutations are applied to `PREFERENCES.md`; the rest are dropped with a logged count.
- [ ] **AC-3.3:** Given the scribe response contains content matching ANY blocking-mitigation rule (forbidden substrings, invalid schema, duplicate, bad id, Unicode bidi/zero-width chars, paths/URLs/emails in statement), When the parser runs, Then that mutation is rejected and logged; other valid mutations in the same response are still applied.
- [ ] **AC-3.4:** Given `mode === 'autonomous-with-checkpoints'`, When the scribe proposes mutations, Then the CLI shows a diff and asks for approval (default: accept) BEFORE writing PREFERENCES.md.
- [ ] **AC-3.5:** Given `mode === 'fully-autonomous'`, When the scribe proposes mutations, Then they are applied without prompt; HISTORY.md records every applied mutation with its provenance (phase, transcript hash).
- [ ] **AC-3.6:** Given any future agent (Analyst, PM, Architect, Dev, etc.) runs, When the orchestrator builds the system prompt, Then `PREFERENCES.md` content is injected as `wrapUntrusted` data, BUT only the `statement` field of each entry — never `why` or `edge-case` (reduces injection budget 3x).
- [ ] **AC-3.7:** Given the scribe is invoked but the LLM call fails (timeout, rate limit, provider error), When the failure happens, Then the cycle continues unaffected; the scribe transcript is saved to `.iagentek/.transcripts/scribe-<phaseId>.md` for debugging.
- [ ] **AC-3.8:** Given a preference exists with `protected: true`, When the scribe attempts `memory:update` or `memory:deprecate` on it, Then the mutation is rejected by the parser regardless of approval mode.
- [ ] **AC-3.9:** Given the Claude Code plugin user runs `/iagentek-context`, When invoked, Then the plugin returns the content of `CONTEXT.md` from the active project.
- [ ] **AC-3.10:** Given the Claude Code plugin user runs `/iagentek-recall <query>`, When invoked, Then the plugin greps `HISTORY.md` (and archives) and returns matching events.

## Blocking security mitigations (non-negotiable for release)

These come from the red-team review. ALL must pass tests before v0.5.0 ships.

1. **B-1:** Parser ONLY accepts `memory:*` blocks from the scribe's direct output. Detection of `memory:*` syntax in any phase transcript triggers a cycle abort with security warning.
2. **B-2:** Schema validation applied to ALL fields (`id`, `category`, `statement`, `why`, `reason`, `edge-case`, `source`, `confidence`, `field`), not just `statement`.
3. **B-3:** `id` must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$`. `category` must be in the closed enum. `field` (for updates) must be in the whitelist `{statement, why, edge-case, status}`. No `__proto__`, no arbitrary keys.
4. **B-4:** Mandatory human diff approval for ALL mutations in `autonomous-with-checkpoints` mode. No CLI flag to disable except via `mode = fully-autonomous` (whole-project setting, not per-cycle).
5. **B-5:** Sanitize Unicode bidi (`‪-‮`, `⁦-⁩`) and zero-width (`​-‍`, `﻿`) characters from all incoming scribe-emitted fields before writing.
6. **B-6:** Preferences flagged `protected: true` (defensive prefs in categories `security`-adjacent — though we have no `security` category, we honor the flag) cannot be `memory:update`'d or `memory:deprecate`'d by the scribe. Only manual edit can remove them.
7. **B-7:** Lockfile `.iagentek/PREFERENCES.lock` during mutation. Detect mtime change between read and write; abort if changed.
8. **B-8:** Only the `statement` field is injected to downstream agents. `why`, `edge-case`, and `reason` are stored but never sent to other LLMs. Reduces poisoned-payload budget by 3x.

## Edge cases
- **Edge-1:** User runs `cycle` with a brownfield analysis of a maliciously-crafted public repo whose README contains team-convention text → analyzed text is in `wrapUntrusted` already; scribe still applies validation; suspicious patterns rejected.
- **Edge-2:** Hostile LLM provider (e.g. local ollama with adversarial model) → DOCUMENTED RESIDUAL RISK. The blocking mitigations defend against semi-honest curators. A fully hostile model can still produce schema-passing but semantically-poisonous mutations. Mode `fully-autonomous` is explicitly NOT recommended with untrusted providers; warning printed at init.
- **Edge-3:** Multi-cycle erosion attack (poisoning split across 10+ cycles) → detector flags N consecutive `memory:update` mutations on the same `id` as suspicious; surfaces in `status` as `⚠ erosion pattern detected on PREF-007`.
- **Edge-4:** Scribe emits a `memory:add` whose `statement` is 60% lexically similar to an existing entry → rejected as duplicate at parse time.
- **Edge-5:** User edits `PREFERENCES.md` while a cycle is running and the scribe is about to mutate → lockfile detection aborts the mutation, scribe transcript preserved for retry.
- **Edge-6:** Claude Code plugin runs `/iagentek-recall` on a project with no HISTORY.md → returns empty result with informative message "no project memory yet — run a cycle first".
- **Edge-7:** Scribe runs but the cycle is in mode `fully-autonomous` AND the LLM provider was the same one that just ran the phase → no isolation; documented in security notes. A second provider for the scribe is a v2 hardening.

## NOT in scope of this release
- Second-opinion curator (different model verifying scribe output).
- Cryptographic integrity hash of `PREFERENCES.md`.
- Quarantine zone (`PREFERENCES.staging.md`) before promoting prefs.
- Automatic deprecation pattern detector across N cycles (basic erosion detection IS in scope; pattern learning is not).
- Per-agent preference subsetting (Dev gets full prefs, Analyst gets none) — v2 optimization.
- `iagentek stats` command — orthogonal feature.
- Aggregated anonymous telemetry — separate decision, requires opt-in flow.

## Dependencies
- Specs that must exist first: v0.4.5, v0.4.6.
- External data/systems: at least one configured LLM provider (any of the 6 supported) capable of structured output. Tested first with `anthropic`, then `claude-cli`, then `openai`. Local `ollama` recommended only for testing, not production preferences (documented).

## Success metrics (post-deploy, aggregated across all 3 releases)

- **M-1:** `time_from_resume_to_first_phase_decision_after_pause` — measured locally per project. Hypothesis: drops by >50% vs. v0.4.4 baseline once user has `CONTEXT.md` + "Welcome back" block.
- **M-2:** `manual_state_inspection_events` — count of times the user reads `state.json` manually (rough proxy: file access timestamps tracked at start of `cycle`). Should approach zero after v0.4.6.
- **M-3:** `scribe_mutation_acceptance_rate` — of all scribe-proposed mutations, % approved by human (interactive mode). Target ≥70%. Below 50% → scribe heuristics are wrong.
- **M-4:** `preferences_reuse_count` — number of times a stored preference appeared in an agent's context injection. Validates that PREFERENCES.md is doing work, not just collecting dust.
- **M-5:** `crash_recovery_success_rate` — % of crashes followed by a successful `resume` that completes a phase without re-prompting the user. Should be 100% in normal cases (excluding genuinely catastrophic disk failures).

All metrics captured locally in `.iagentek/.stats.json`. Optional opt-in share via future `iagentek stats --share` command (NOT in scope of this feature spec).

---

## Backwards compatibility

All three releases are additive for projects created in v0.4.4 or earlier. The `bootstrap` step in v0.4.6 silently reconstructs `CONTEXT.md` from existing artifacts. v0.5.0's scribe activates only on the next approved checkpoint after upgrade; older checkpoints are not retroactively curated. No `iagentek migrate` command, no user-visible migration step.

The only API change is in `CheckpointManager.run()` signature (returns `{ decision, notes }` instead of just `decision`). The orchestrator is the only known consumer in the codebase. External consumers (any third-party using `@iagentek/core` directly) get a compile error at upgrade — documented in the v0.5.0 changelog and migration note.
